questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The world's happiest countries and why they're happy
Amsterdam's 'doughnut' model for a better city
How to make delicious doughnuts at home
Why designer jeans are so expensive to buy
questions.why: They discuss how Amsterdam uses the idea of a ring doughnut as a model for sustainability.

questions.q: Does Rob think utopia really exists?
options: Yes, he thinks it already exists in Amsterdam
Yes, he believes it exists in Finland
He is sure it will exist within a few years
Probably not, but it's something people aim for
questions.why: Rob says 'probably not, but it's something we aspire to create'.

questions.q: In the doughnut model, what does the hole in the middle represent?
options: People who don't have the basic things they need
Too much pressure on the planet's natural resources
Cities that are growing too fast for their transport
Money that is wasted by governments on big projects
questions.why: Rob says the idea is not to leave anyone in the hole, falling short on the essentials of life.

questions.q: What happens if we go beyond the outer ring of the doughnut?
options: Everyone becomes richer
People lose their jobs
The planet is put under too much pressure
Cities become too small for everyone
questions.why: Rob says beyond the outer ring we put so much pressure on the planet it can cause climate change.

questions.q: How does Kate Raworth say Amsterdam wants to change how it builds?
options: By importing cheaper building materials from abroad
By reusing construction materials already in the city
By building much taller buildings in the city centre
By stopping all new building work for ten years
questions.why: She says instead of new raw materials, they ask how to reuse materials already in the city.

questions.q: What is good about Mud Jeans' recycled jeans, according to the presenters?
options: They save cotton, chemicals and water
They are cheap enough for everyone to buy
They are made only from new cotton
They never wear out
questions.why: Rob says they may not be affordable for all, but reduce cotton, chemicals and water and create jobs.

questions.q: What point does Bert van Son make about making jeans?
options: Machines make better and cheaper jeans than people do
Jeans should always be made as fast as possible
Workers in jeans factories don't really need medical care
You can't make nice jeans if the workers are treated badly
questions.why: He says if you mistreat the people making your jeans, 'you will never be able to make nice jeans'.

questions.q: What does Bert van Son mean when he says making clothing 'has to become human again'?
options: Clothes should all be made slowly by hand at home
Clothes should look more natural and be less colourful
It should involve compassion and respect for workers
Only people, not computers, should design new clothes
questions.why: Georgina explains he means being someone with compassion, feelings and respect for others.
